provenance.title: Antenatal classification tables — anaemia in pregnancy
provenance.primarySource: WHO recommendations on antenatal care (2016); WHO haemoglobin thresholds to diagnose anaemia (2011/2024)
provenance.why: Anaemia in pregnancy is graded, not binary, and the grade changes what happens: mild is oral iron and review, moderate is investigation and treatment, severe near term is a transfusion decision and a delivery-place decision. A single 'anaemic yes/no' flag loses exactly the distinction that matters.

sourceVerification.vendoredArtefact: docs/reference/who-dak/smart-anc — haemoglobin data element; the grade cut-offs are WHO published thresholds
sourceVerification.note: The severe/moderate/mild cut-offs are WHO published haemoglobin thresholds. The trimester adjustment (the diagnostic threshold is 11.0 g/dL in the first and third trimesters and 10.5 in the second) is applied by scoring the reassuring row against a trimester-selected band. Cut-offs pending ministry ratification; blocksRatification stays true.

tables.name: Anaemia in pregnancy
sourceRefs: WHO recommendations on antenatal care (2016) — anaemia
WHO haemoglobin thresholds to diagnose anaemia

tiers.name: Severe anaemia
tiers.action: Haemoglobin below 7 g/dL. Assess for decompensation, investigate the cause, and make a transfusion decision. Near term, this also decides where she should deliver — she needs a facility that can transfuse.
treatments: Plan delivery at a facility that can transfuse

adaptation.whoStatement: Haemoglobin below 7 g/dL in pregnancy is severe anaemia requiring urgent assessment and a transfusion decision.

tiers.name: Moderate anaemia
tiers.action: Haemoglobin 7.0–9.9 g/dL. Investigate the cause — iron deficiency is common but not the only one — and treat. Recheck the response.

adaptation.whoStatement: Haemoglobin 70–99 g/L is moderate anaemia requiring treatment and investigation of cause.

tiers.name: Mild anaemia
tiers.action: Mild anaemia for this trimester (below 11.0 g/dL in the first or third trimester, below 10.5 in the second, and at or above 10). Start or continue oral iron and folic acid and recheck.
treatments: Recheck haemoglobin at the next contact

adaptation.whoStatement: The haemoglobin threshold for anaemia in pregnancy is 11.0 g/dL in the first and third trimesters and 10.5 g/dL in the second.
adaptation.nationalStatement: Adopted as published, with the trimester threshold applied by a gestational-age band so the reassuring cut-off is not a single number applied to the whole pregnancy.

tiers.name: No anaemia for this trimester
tiers.action: Haemoglobin at or above the threshold for this trimester. Continue routine iron and folic acid supplementation.
treatments: Routine iron and folic acid supplementation
sourceRefs: WHO recommendations on antenatal care (2016) — iron supplementation

adaptation.whoStatement: Daily oral iron and folic acid supplementation is recommended for pregnant women.
evidenceRefs: WHO recommendations on antenatal care (2016) — iron supplementation

testCases.name: Hb 10.6 in the third trimester is mild (below 11.0)
Hb 10.6 in the second trimester is NOT anaemia (threshold 10.5)
